statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-5713: The asyncio introspection tools (python -m asyncio ps and python -m asyncio pstree) used offset tables read from the target process without validating them, so a privileged process connecting to a malicious Python process through the remote debugging feature could be made to read and write out-of-bounds addresses. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/148178 (3.14 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/316f6265b7f9ca4ffed5346b747475ef1943f35d), first released in CPython 3.14.5; see https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/OG4RHARYSNIE22GGOMVMCRH76L5HKPLM/; https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-5713. Checked the _remote_debugging extension module in every published build, 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.10-r4, of the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.14 package on x86_64 and aarch64 for the offset-table validation the fix adds (its 'Invalid debug offsets' and 'Invalid AsyncioDebug offsets' errors). 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.4-r3 lack the fix; 3.14.4-r4 is the first published build that has it and carries a DHI backport of the upstream fix, ahead of the upstream release, and every later build carries it.

Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/148178 (3.14 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/316f6265b7f9ca4ffed5346b747475ef1943f35d), first released in CPython 3.14.5; see https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/OG4RHARYSNIE22GGOMVMCRH76L5HKPLM/; https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-5713.
